title: The second is a count of cesium microwave oscillations
summary: NIST says atomic clocks count 9,192,631,770 oscillations of a cesium transition and call that interval a second.
body: NIST's page on the second says the second is currently defined using cesium atoms, which absorb and emit microwave radiation at a specific frequency, and that atomic clocks count 9,192,631,770 of those oscillations and call the elapsed interval a second. The second is a human convention anchored to an atomic frequency. It is the base of the metre definition as well.
